environment.description: Same Ktor service deployed on identical ECS Fargate infrastructure. The ALB has an associated AWS WAF WebACL but it only contains rate-limiting rules (AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet with SizeRestrictions_BODY action set to COUNT mode, not BLOCK). The key difference is the Envoy sidecar proxy configuration: it injects a Content-Security-Policy response header on all text/html responses with the directive `script-src 'self' 'sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC' https://cdn.example.com`. Additionally, all <script> tags referencing cdn.example.com in the HTML template have integrity='sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC' crossorigin='anonymous' attributes added by a Lua filter in the Envoy pipeline that pattern-matches on cdn.example.com src attributes before forwarding the response body. Inline scripts without a matching hash in the CSP are blocked by the browser. The injected Object.assign(Object.prototype, ...) payload is an inline script without a pre-computed hash in the CSP allowlist, so the browser refuses to execute it.

config.network: ALB with AWS WAF (rate-limit rules only, body size in COUNT mode)
config.envoy_sidecar: v1.28, Lua HTTP filter injects SRI attributes on CDN script tags
config.csp_injection: Envoy response header filter adds script-src with sha384 hashes for known scripts
config.inline_script_policy: no unsafe-inline, no unsafe-eval; only pre-hashed inline scripts allowed
config.sri_enforcement: browser-side via integrity attribute on external scripts
